tip.title: Somebody wanted... but... so... then
tip.text: A SUMMARY gives only the most important parts, in order, in your own words. Leave out small details. For a story, use this frame: SOMEBODY (who?) WANTED (goal) BUT (problem) SO (what they did) THEN (how it ended). A good summary makes sense to someone who never read the story.

passage.title: When the Music Stopped
passage.text:
The Northside crew had practiced for two months for the city dance battle. They wanted to make the top three. The prize was ten thousand pesos and a slot in the regional finals.

They were the sixth crew to perform. Thirty seconds into their routine, the speaker cut out. Silence. The crowd went quiet. Dave froze in the middle of a move. For a second, nobody knew what to do.

Then Kaye started clapping a beat. Loud, steady, on time. The rest of the crew picked it up. They finished the whole routine to the sound of their own hands and feet. By the end, the crowd was clapping with them.

The sound team fixed the speaker, and the judges let them perform again with music. But the judges said the first run was the one they would remember. Northside placed second. On the jeepney home, nobody talked about the prize money. They talked about the clapping.

words.meaning: a set of moves performed in a fixed order
words.example: The crew practiced their routine every day.

words.meaning: suddenly stopped moving, usually from shock or fear
words.example: He froze when he saw the snake.

words.meaning: covering a whole region, bigger than one city
words.example: She won the regional science contest.

items.prompt: Which is the BEST summary of the story?
choices: Northside rode a jeepney home and did not talk about money.
Northside wanted a top-three finish, but the speaker died mid-routine, so they finished by clapping their own beat, and they placed second.
Kaye clapped a beat and the crowd joined in.
The sound team fixed the speaker and the crew performed again.
items.why: It has the somebody, the goal, the problem, the fix, and the ending. The others are single details.

items.prompt: Which detail should be LEFT OUT of a summary?
choices: They were the sixth crew to perform.
They finished the routine by clapping.
items.why: Being sixth in line does not change what happens. The other choices are key events.

items.prompt: In the frame "Somebody wanted... but...", what is the BUT (the problem)?
choices: The speaker cut out during their routine.
items.why: The problem is the dead speaker. Wanting the top three is the goal; the rest is the ending.

items.prompt: Why did the crew keep dancing after the music stopped?
choices: Kaye clapped a beat and the others followed it.
items.why: "Then Kaye started clapping a beat... The rest of the crew picked it up."

items.prompt: Why did the judges say the first run was the one they would remember?
choices: The crew showed courage and teamwork by finishing without music.
items.why: Finishing a routine with no music, on a clapped beat, is harder and braver than dancing to a track.

items.prompt: Put the events of the story in order.
items.why: Silence came first, then Kaye's beat, then the crowd joined, and the placing came at the end.

items.prompt: Why did the crowd go quiet thirty seconds into the routine?
choices: The crew stopped dancing on purpose.
The speaker cut out, and there was silence.
items.why: "Thirty seconds into their routine, the speaker cut out. Silence. The crowd went quiet."

items.prompt: "Dave froze in the middle of a move." What does this show about Dave?
choices: He was shocked and did not know what to do.
items.why: To freeze is to stop from shock. The next sentence confirms it: "For a second, nobody knew what to do."

items.prompt: What happened BECAUSE the sound team fixed the speaker?
choices: The judges let the crew perform again with music.
items.why: "The sound team fixed the speaker, and the judges let them perform again with music."

items.prompt: Why did nobody talk about the prize money on the jeepney home?
choices: They were sad that they lost.
They were prouder of finishing without music than of the money.
The coach told them to stay quiet.
items.why: They placed second and won money, yet "they talked about the clapping." The moment they made together mattered more than the prize.
